title: Player clicked 'Recycle Rune -> Order Rune (ready)'. In the AFTER state the Order Rune was only exhausted (+1 energy, 1->2) but was still in the rune zone (runeCount 2, rune deck still 10) and no Order power was added (power {}); recycleRune for that rune is still listed in available moves. The actual recycle only landed later (visible by step 4: power.order=1, rune gone). The UI implements panel-
expected: Source matches the claim exactly. The action panel's 'Recycle Rune -> <rune> (ready)' sub-item is wired to quickRecycleRune (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/actions.js:363-368: `splitByState && !isExh(m) ... ? \`quickRecycleRune(${JSON.stringify(m.params?.runeId)}, this)\``). quickRecycleRune (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/interactions.js:427-456) dispatches executeMove(exhaustMove) first (line 441), then runs a client-side poll `tryRecycle` that re-checks findCard(runeId).meta.exhausted and sends recycleRune only once seen, retrying `if (++tries <= 10) setTimeout(tryRecycle, 100)` (line 454) — i.e. two separate dispatches with a ~1s window after which the recycle is silently abandoned. Trace corroborates: step 3 (click-sub 'Order Rune (ready)') shows energy 1->2, Order Rune exhausted but still in runePool, power {}, recycleRune for that rune still in moves; step 4 shows power.order=1 and the rune gone, so the recycle landed as a later separate frame.
